runtimeFlags: DFlash n7; XPU graphs on; fp16 KV; --no-enable-prefix-caching; gptq/float16; gpu-mem-util 0.90; max-num-seqs 1; max-model-len 262144; router patch applied
notes:
FULL 262,144-TOKEN CONTEXT, functionally verified - not just a successful boot. Served on vllm/vllm-openai-xpu:v0.30.0 with the router patch registered as the custom runtime for this entry; that patch is REQUIRED here, because without it the engine dies at init above max-model-len 16384 (see the custom runtime notes). Engine-reported KV pool at gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 with the DFlash draft loaded: 348,249 tokens, i.e. 1.33x a full 262,144-token request, fp16 KV, max-num-seqs 1. Functional proof of the context: needle-in-haystack with a unique fact planted at 10%, 50% and 90% depth of a 250,044-token prompt, greedy - 3/3 retrieved correctly, zero failures. 

HEADLINE CELL (decodeTps): p512 prompt, C1, greedy - 228.34 tok/s, median of 3, spread 228.29-228.53 across reps, window acceptance 60.3%, TTFT 105 ms, isolated engine prefill 5,339 tok/s. Engine-only decode for the same cell is 229.19 tok/s. All at a 230 W configured power cap. 

COMPARABLE CELL: at p2048/g128 - the cell and method used by the existing 2026-08-13 entry - this same build measures 200.75 tok/s (median of 3, 197.27-201.05, acceptance 55.0%, all reps byte-identical), versus 186.61 in that entry. Quoting 228.34 instead of 200.75 is not like-for-like with the 186.61: it is a shorter prompt, and prompt length drives speculative acceptance and therefore decode rate. Both cells are measured and labelled; compare to the p2048/g128 figure if you want an apples-to-apples delta. 

PREFILL: promptTps 10197 is the isolated engine metric (vllm:request_prefill_time_seconds delta) at 8208 prompt tokens, median of 3, TTFT 0.82 s - NOT a prompt_tokens/TTFT proxy. Measured across prompt lengths on this stack at 230 W: 5,339 (p512), 9,198 (p2048), 10,197 (p8192), 8,892 (p32768), 5,585 (p131072), 3,817 (p250000). Prefill peaks in the 2-8K band and declines on both sides, so the 10,197 figure is the peak of that curve, not a typical value. 

DECODE vs CONTEXT on this build at 230 W (real wikitext workload, median of 3): 228.34 at 512, 200.75 at 2,048, 74.82 at 32,768, 25.97 at 131,072, 22.26 at 250,000 tokens. Decode falls about 6x from 512 to 250K; that is the per-step cost of attending over a long KV and is inherent to running at range, not a tuning failure. 

SPECULATION: the draft does NOT degrade with context. A controlled test holding the generation task constant and varying only haystack length gives window acceptance of 62.5% at 512, 63.5% at 32,768, 60.3% at 131,072 and 62.5% at 250,000 tokens - flat. An uncontrolled ladder that varied the prompt together with the length reported 17.5% at 131K; that is content variance, not a length effect, and must not be read as a drafter collapse. The draft window optimum is also context-independent: n=7 beats n=3 and n=15 at every length tested (at 131,072 tokens: 60.6 vs 39.8 vs 33.9 tok/s). Note n=3 has the HIGHER acceptance (74-78% vs 62%) and is still slower everywhere - tokens-per-step sets throughput, not hit rate, so a shallow window is never the fix for low acceptance. 

HONESTY NOTES: the target is a local symmetric GPTQ INT4 G64 conversion and the draft is a local NVFP4-to-BF16 reconstruction, not official HF quants. Results are from a single card of a 2x B70 rig. With the DFlash draft loaded only one 262,144-token request fits concurrently; dropping the draft raises the KV pool to 1,318,604 tokens (5.03x) at the cost of speculative decoding. The unpatched stock build is faster on short contexts but cannot serve long context at all, so these numbers are not a like-for-like comparison against the 150 W and 230 W stock entries - they are the cost of having range. Evidence, raw JSON and the context/window charts are in the cookbook page listed under evidenceUrl.
